scope: NNTrain value Verify exact saved holdout
authority: Repository software and executable synthetic regression only
defect: Verify ignored persisted split IDs and rebuilt a split from its own seed; omitted or conflicting seeds could evaluate training games as validation. Compatible but different datasets were also admitted as original holdout.
fix: Require original dataset SHA256; load nonempty unique disjoint training/validation ID sets which partition the dataset exactly. Always use saved validation IDs; optional seed must parse and match the recorded seed. Missing/invalid legacy split metadata fails closed.

worker.verification: Primary verified both source hashes/line counts and every literal citation. Worker purpose prose and unresolved items are bounded inventory, not independent semantic or executable proof.

validation_environment.source: Clean HEAD src/BotSim/NNTrain plus three scoped files. Existing unrelated dirty probe changes excluded.
validation_environment.runtime_data_note: Exact runtime bytes satisfy native-default proof; LF-normalized runtime content matches HEAD. Matrix provenance uses exact Git bytes separately.

remaining: Software saved-holdout reproduction only; no card/native rule certification, throughput or strength claim.
Verify now requires the bound original dataset and saved split metadata. Models without complete split metadata require retraining for this command; inference consumers are unchanged.
No independent new-dataset evaluation command is introduced. ValueTrainingContract.RequireDataset remains a distribution-compatibility check; Verify additionally enforces the original dataset hash.
Metadata and sidecars are unsigned provenance, not tamper-proof artifacts. Joint malicious rewriting or a valid but falsified partition is outside this validation.
Synthetic four-game tests cover win/pair execution and two sampling modes; single-game holdouts have no ranking pairs, so no pair-learning efficacy is claimed.
Random training splits remain random when no seed is provided; saved IDs reproduce each resulting model holdout. No old evidence bindings are refreshed.
